With the consent of both sides, this Writ Petition is taken up for final disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. This writ petition is filed to quash the impugned letter issued by the first respondent in letter No.558/LA1[1]/05-2, dated 11.03.2005 and consequently direct the fourth respondent to deposit the compensation by calculating as per Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 [Central Act 30 of 2013] in so far relate to the petitioners lands situated at No.63, Madam Village, Tiruthani Taluk, Tiruvallur District to the extent of 4 acres 7 cents.

sentences.text:
3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Government Advocates appearing for the respondents and perused the materials available on record.
4.
The case of the petitioners is that the lands of the petitioners have been acquired by the Government to construct cottage in Tiruthani Temple.
The grievance of the petitioners is that the compensation amount deposited before the reference Court has not been disbursed to them.
However, challenge has been made to the communication of the authorities dated 11.03.2005.
The communication sent by the respondents indicate the manner in which the amount has to be deposited and compensation for the land acquired shall be paid.

5. At this stage, this Court is of the view that the communication cannot be challenged after a lapse of 19 years and the compensation amount shall be disbursed to the petitioners keeping in mind the judgment of the Constitutional https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Bench of this Court.

Hence, the R.S.Prakash Rao vs The Secretary To Government on 3 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119429486/
